extracted.intended_audience: general readers, parents and teachers interested in child health and sleep hygiene (readers of Popular Science Monthly)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and prescriptions about sleep: how much sleep various ages need, environmental and behavioral measures to promote healthy sleep, bedding/bedroom recommendations, and remedies/anti-patterns for insomnia and sleepless children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of sleep by age and condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribes typical sleep-duration targets: children under ten should choose between eight and ten hours; in later years seven hours minimum and nine hours maximum for healthy children; sickly children and consumptives should have no restriction (carte blanche).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requisite amount depends on temperament and occupation as well as age. Newborns and infants require more sleep proportional to physiological waste; weakly babies need sleep more than food. Habitual deficiency undermines health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow infants to sleep to full satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Nurslings should be permitted to sleep to their full satisfaction; do not disturb a child's slumber while regular breathing indicates healthy repose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three or four nursings in 24 hours suffice; avoid coaxing infants to overfeed. There is little danger of oversleeping a moderately warmed, well-ventilated baby; hunger will awaken the infant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nursery and bedroom arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: When space allows, the nursery (play-room) and the infant's sleeping/dormitory should be two separate apartments: play-room sunny, bedroom shady and sequestered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Next to outdoor exercise, silence and subdued light are the best hypnotics. Keep bedroom cool and quiet; locate dormitory on the coolest side of the house (north side) and far from the kitchen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid artificial stupor and narcotics for insomnia
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overcome insomnia by cradling, rocking to stupefaction, or by using narcotics/opium; stupefaction is not proper sleep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lethargy induced by rocking is akin to sea-sickness; narcotics merely benumb rather than restore healthy sleep. Prefer natural measures like ventilation and rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and treat causes of child sleeplessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Different symptoms point to different causes: impatient turning suggests room is too stuffy/warm; long wakefulness with squalling and petulance indicates acidity in the stomach (overfeeding/soothing-syrup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For acidity let the child exercise on the floor; in malignant cases skip a meal or give water instead of milk. After croup, leave child undisturbed with half-open window; rest and slow deep breathing aid recovery more than medicine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use habit and schedule to teach sleep-wake association
rubrics_metrics.description: Mothers should perform nursing/fondling in daytime so children learn to associate darkness with silence and slumber; habit can train children to sleep and wake at set times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow children to rise with the sun; if drowsy they will go to bed earlier next evening. Fixed hours of sleep can overcome neuralgia and improve mental control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not curtail sleep for extra study
rubrics_metrics.description: Stinting children in sleep to gain hours for study is counterproductive; such children are never wide-awake and learn far less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A wide-awake child will learn more in one hour than a day-dreamer in ten. Habitual sleep deficiency leads to headache, feverish heat, mental decline, and long-term harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support midday naps and biphasic sleep in hot seasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow or encourage noon naps/siestas, especially in hot climates or during dog-days; consider increasing noontide recess to at least three hours to allow for a digestive siesta.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many peoples and animals take noontide rest; prohibiting daytime sleep in hot weather is harmful. If possible postpone principal meal to end of day or allow children to rest from 12 to 3 p.m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bedding and mattress recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend a hard, broad mattress or well-stuffed straw tick as best; prefer a woolen blanket over a linen bedsheet rather than a quilt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid thick bolsters/pillows that bend the head or aggravate respiratory distress. Woven-wire mattresses recommended for cleanliness and durability; for those uncomfortable sleeping flat, slightly raise the head-end rather than use a thick bolster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summer sleep: cool the head and bedroom
rubrics_metrics.description: In hot weather reduce bedclothing, cool the bedroom (open windows), use a hard smooth mattress and linen sheets, and have a light supper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: George Combe recommends glazed brick floors and frequent sprinkling; in very hot nights use tubs with ice where feasible. Consider ability to change beds (cool vs warm) if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper bedroom placement and window orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Bedrooms should ideally be the coolest room in the house (nearest the north side and farthest from kitchen); east windows make good bedroom fronts for evening shade and morning sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where climate varies extremely by season, varying bedroom location with season could be beneficial. In large houses northerly location cooler overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warm extremities to promote sleep
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting warmth in the feet/limbs (hot foot-bath, chafing arms/legs, warming feet toward embers) can divert blood from the head and have a somniferous effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is based on the idea that decreasing cerebral blood-circulation favors sleep; used practically by trappers, Swiss mountaineers (foot-sacks), and soldiers in bivouac.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and monotony can be hypnotic
rubrics_metrics.description: Listening to distant music, river ripple, or repetition of monotonous sounds aids sleep; some sensorial stimulation is more favorable to repose than total silence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kant's and Burton's anecdotal methods are cited though laborious mental tasks can also induce sleep; simpler natural remedies (outdoor exercise, fresh air) are preferred before resorting to medicinal/superstitious cures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietary influence on dreams and sleep quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Dietary 'sins' (heavy or irritating foods like blood sausage, sauerkraut, pork-fritters, eel-pie) can provoke vivid dreams or nightmares; light supper recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Melodramatic dreams may indicate irritating ingesta; adjust diet and promote outdoor exercise and laxative diets as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleeping alone for older children
rubrics_metrics.description: It's recommended that children over ten years sleep alone; this is supported as an etiquette rule with valid health reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sleeping alone helps avoid crowding and heat; Franklin even recommended two beds per individual when affordable to change to a cool bed in hot nights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow flexibility for working/teaching adults
rubrics_metrics.description: If obliged to work/teach all day, an individual may skip midday food and rest under shade, but parents who educate at home should give either long summer vacation or afternoon recess for rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where necessary, compromise is acceptable, but preserve opportunities for rest; children of parents who can afford it should rest from noon until three or sleep if preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superstition against night/morning air
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuke superstition that night or morning air is injurious; fresh night-wind revitalizes bedroom air and is beneficial after hot days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to cool night air after hot days is healing; cultural pruning of outdoor activity after dark is criticized when it leads to suffocating unventilated bedrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrophone as adjunct to spectroscope (experimental method note)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrophone should remain a mere adjunct to the spectroscope rather than replace it, though it has a wide and independent usefulness in investigating absorption spectra in the ultra-red.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results presented are preliminary and incomplete — early experiments are valuable though more mature research is needed. This is an experimental-method caution rather than definitive claim.
